1.title: For All Debts Public and Private

probes.text: In session, Tony says the only ways out of his line of work are dead or in the can.
Chris sits with his mother in her kitchen, the talk turning to his long-dead father.
Meadow drifts around the house with no motivation, and Melfi recommends a therapist for her to Tony.
At a pro-Italian luncheon, the guest speaker's jabs at mobbed-up Italians leave the wives at the table insulted.
A Native American group picketing the local Columbus Day parade has Tony's crew taking the whole thing personally.
Silvio keeps grousing about disrespect toward Italians until Tony snaps at the whole idea of victimized groups.
Furio throws a housewarming party at his newly bought house, with guests dancing to Italian music.
Carmela goes along to look at houses with Furio, offering opinions on what he should buy.
Melfi tells Kupferberg that her son has started acting out while away at college.
Late at night Tony sits alone in the stall with the ailing racehorse, murmuring to keep her calm.
Ralphie's racehorse keeps crossing the line first, and Tony keeps asking for a bigger share of the winnings.
Janice inserts herself into Bobby's household, warning that Junior will drop him if he stays lost in grief.
Tony spends the week doing uncharacteristically generous favors and kindnesses for various people in his life.
A group of armed teenagers is sent to frighten the occupants out of a run-down house.
A relative of Carmela's pitches Tony on a real estate scheme he could get a piece of.
Paulie's mother moves into a retirement community, where a clique of the other residents gives her the cold shoulder.
A portrait of Tony posing with the racehorse Pie-O-My is commissioned from a painter.
Furio flies back to Naples for his father's funeral and spends time with his uncle there.
Paulie hangs the horse portrait in his own home, having it repainted so Tony wears a Napoleon-like uniform.
A new home nurse turns up to look after Junior, arranged through Svetlana Kirilenko.
Furio is back from Italy, and Carmela keeps inventing reasons to drop by and see him.
Janice sits Bobby's frightened children down with an ouija board, which does nothing to calm them.
In a dream, Tony stands outside a strange house, telling someone he is there about a stonemason job.
Tony dreams of Carmela behind the wheel of Johnny Soprano's old car, with passengers in the back.
